slot.brief: Find the domain of a composite function combining a square root and a logarithm; intersect conditions.

verdicts.working: For \(\sqrt{\ln(3-x)}\), require \(\ln(3-x)\ge 0\), so \(x\le 2\). For \(\ln\sqrt{x+1}\), require \(x+1>0\), so \(x>-1\). The intersection is \((-1,2]\).

working:
$\sqrt{\ln(3-x)}:\ 3-x>0,\ \ln(3-x)\geq0\Rightarrow x\leq2.$ Also $\ln\sqrt{x+1}$ requires $\sqrt{x+1}>0\Rightarrow x>-1.$ Domain: $(-1,2].$

Independent check: For \(\sqrt{\ln(3-x)}\), require \(\ln(3-x)\ge 0\), so \(x\le 2\). For \(\ln\sqrt{x+1}\), require \(x+1>0\), so \(x>-1\). The intersection is \((-1,2]\).
solution:
For $\sqrt{\ln(3-x)}$, require $\ln(3-x)\ge 0$, giving $x\le 2$. For $\ln\sqrt{x+1}$, require $x+1>0$, giving $x>-1$.
$$\text{Domain}=(-1,2]$$
